rubric: DATABASES / AGGREGATES, JOINS AND SUBQUERIES / CHAPTER 6

slides.title: Data in different tables
slides.main: JOIN glues rows of two tables by a condition.

captions: Customers and orders live in different tables
customer_id in an order points to the customer's id
JOIN glues related rows into one: a customer next to their order

slides.title: Each with each
slides.main: Without a condition JOIN gives all pairs of rows: n × m.

captions: Two tables: two customers and three sizes
Without a condition we get every pair: 2 × 3 = 6 rows
With customers and orders: 4 × 3 = 12 rows, only 3 meaningful

slides.title: INNER JOIN
slides.main: INNER JOIN … ON keeps only pairs for which the condition is true.

captions: INNER JOIN … ON: the condition links a foreign key to a primary key
Pairs are found where o.customer_id = c.id; Vera and Gleb have none
Only matched pairs get into the result

lines: JOIN orders o ON o.cust = c.id;
JOIN orders o ON o.cust = c.id;
JOIN orders o ON o.cust = c.id;

slides.title: Names and aliases
slides.main: If a column is in both tables, write table.column.

captions: id is in both customers and orders — the database can't tell which one
Put the table name and a dot before the column
Short aliases c and o after table names keep the query compact

lines: FROM customers c JOIN orders o

frames.text: c and o are table aliases

slides.title: ON and WHERE
slides.main: For INNER JOIN a condition in ON and in WHERE is equivalent.

captions: First we get all customer–order pairs
WHERE keeps orders over 10,000
For INNER JOIN the condition can move to ON — same result

lines: FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.cust = c.id
FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.cust = c.id
FROM customers c JOIN orders o

slides.title: LEFT JOIN
slides.main: LEFT JOIN keeps all rows of the left table; fills the missing with NULL.

captions: INNER JOIN loses customers with no orders — Vera and Gleb are gone
LEFT JOIN keeps all customers from the left table
Where there is no pair, right-table columns are filled with NULL

lines: FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON …
FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON …
FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON …

slides.title: Who has no pair
slides.main: LEFT JOIN … WHERE right.key IS NULL finds rows with no pair.

captions: LEFT JOIN: customers without orders have an empty right side
WHERE o.id IS NULL keeps only them: Vera and Gleb
NOT EXISTS gives the same result: no order for this customer

lines: LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.cust = c.id;
LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.cust = c.id
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders o

slides.title: LEFT JOIN trap
slides.main: A condition on the right table in WHERE turns LEFT JOIN into INNER.

captions: LEFT JOIN, but the order status is checked in WHERE
Vera and Gleb have status = NULL — condition fails, rows vanish
Moved the condition to ON: customers kept, other orders dropped

lines: FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o
FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o
FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o

slides.title: RIGHT and FULL
slides.main: RIGHT mirrors LEFT, FULL keeps rows of both tables.

captions: RIGHT is a mirrored LEFT: right-table rows are kept
FULL keeps rows of both tables, the missing is NULL on both sides
CROSS — all pairs, no condition

slides.title: Chain of tables
slides.main: Tables are joined one by one: each JOIN is its own link.

captions: To see who bought what, you need customers, orders, lines and products
Join one by one: each new table adds its own link in ON
Each result row is a customer, an order and a purchased product

frames.text: JOIN … ON … JOIN … ON … JOIN … ON …

slides.title: Row multiplication
slides.main: After JOIN one row can multiply: aggregates get inflated.

captions: An order of 100 with three lines
After JOIN there are three rows, and total repeats in each
SUM(o.total) = 300 instead of 100; aggregate before joining or over unique orders

slides.title: Self-join
slides.main: A table can be joined to itself — use different aliases.

captions: Each employee has boss_id — the boss's id from the same table
Take the table twice under aliases e and b
Each employee next to their boss; Olga has none — needs LEFT JOIN

lines: JOIN employees b ON e.boss_id = b.id
LEFT JOIN employees b ON e.boss_id = b.id

slides.title: Summary
slides.main: INNER drops unmatched, LEFT keeps them; link condition goes in ON.

captions: INNER, LEFT, RIGHT, FULL, CROSS — kinds of joins
Link in ON; right-table filter under LEFT in ON; watch for multiplication
Next topic — subqueries
